 Index Outlook: Staying firmly bullish
 Supports are there to limit the downside and take the indices higher
 By Gurumurthy K 
 Updated - November 14, 2026 at 09:54 PM. 
 | 
 bl. research bureau
 × Share
 WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/portfolio/technical-analysis/index-outlook-staying-firmly-bullish/article71701225.ece Copy Nifty 50 and Sensex sustained higher and stable all through the week. The expected corrective fall did not happen. Nifty Bank index on the other hand has risen sharply for the second consecutive week. The expected rise to 61,000 on the Nifty Bank index has happened much faster than expected.
 Overall, the outlook continues to remain positive. The Indian benchmark indices can go further higher from here. Any pull-back move will be short-lived. Good supports are there to limit the downside.
 FPIs Buy
 The Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) continued to buy the Indian equities for the fourth consecutive week. Their quantum of purchase was also strong for the second consecutive week. The equity segment saw a net inflow of about $4.82 billion. The FPIs have pumped in about $10 billion in just the last three weeks. If this trend continues, then there are good chances for the Sensex and Nifty to scale new highs in the coming months.
 Video Credit: Businessline Nifty 50 (25,144.30)
 Short-term view: Support is there in the 24,950-24,900 region which can limit the downside if Nifty dips from here. As long as the Nifty stays above 24,900, the bias will continue to remain positive. Nifty can rise to 25,850-26,000.
 In case the index breaks below 24,900, a fall to 24,750 or 24,500 can be seen first. Thereafter, a fresh rise can take the index up to 25,000 and higher eventually. In this case, the rise to 26,000 may get delayed.
 Medium-term view: The broader 22,000-26,500 range is intact. Nifty is heading higher towards the upper end of this range. A test of 26,500 looks likely in the medium term. We retain our long-term bullish bias as well. Nifty can breach 26,500 eventually. Such a break can take it higher towards 28,000 and 30,000 in the long term.
 In case the index fails to break above 26,500, then the broader range can continue to remain intact. In that case, a fall to 25,000 and even lower can be seen. Ideally, Nifty has to decline below 22,000 to prove our long-term bullish view wrong.
 Nifty Bank (61,034.10)
 Short-term view: An immediate resistance is around 61,550. Failure to rise past this resistance can trigger a corrective fall to 59,850 first. Thereafter, a fresh rise can take the index higher breaking above this resistance towards 66,000 in the short term.
 In case the index manages to surpass 61,550 from here itself, then the rise to 66,000 can happen straightaway.
 Medium-term view: The broader uptrend is intact. The rise last week has strengthened the case for a quicker rally to 68,000-69,000 that we have mentioned here to happen over the long term.
 Cluster of supports are there in the 57,000-56,000 region. We can now expect the Nifty Bank index to sustain above 56,000 itself. A strong trigger might now be needed to break below 56,000.
 Also from a long-term perspective, 51,000-50,000 is a strong support zone. Our bullish view will go wrong only if the index declines below 50,000. That looks unlikely at the moment.
 Sensex (81,592.45)
 Short-term view: Key support is in the 81,000-80,500 region. Any dip from current levels can be limited to 80,500. A fresh rise anywhere from the 81,000-80,500 region can take the Sensex up to 83,500-84,000 in the short term.
 In case the Sensex breaks below 80,500, then an extended fall to 79,000 can be seen. Thereafter the index can rise back and go up again. In this case, the rise to 84,000 will get delayed.
 Medium-term view:  The broader 71,000-86,000 range remains intact. Within that, the Sensex is now heading towards the upper end of the range. A rise to 86,000 can be seen in the medium term.
 We see high chances for the Sensex to breach 86,000 eventually. Such a break can take the Sensex higher to 90,000 initially and then to 94,000 eventually in the long term.
 Failure to breach 86,000 can keep the broad sideways range intact and drag the index down to 80,000 and lower. Sensex has to decline below 71,000 to negate our long-term bullish outlook
 Nifty Midcap 150 (22,681.25)
 The index sustained above 22,000 as expected and has risen well for the third consecutive week. That keeps the broader bullish view intact.
 Immediate resistance is at 22,820 which is holding well for now. Failure to rise past this hurdle can trigger a corrective fall 22,450 or even 22,000 in the short term. However, a fall beyond 22,000 is unlikely.
 A break above 22,820 can take the Nifty Midcap 150 index higher to 23,700 and 24,400 in the short term. An eventual break above 24,400 can boost the momentum. Such a break will then clear the way for a rally to 28,000 in the long term.
 Nifty Smallcap 250 (17,940.55)
 The rise to 18,000 has happened in line with our expectation.  Resistance is around 18,050, which is holding well for now. A pull back move from here if seen can test 17,800 or 17,600. A fall beyond 17,600 looks less likely at the moment. Also, 17,000 is a strong support, which is likely to limit the downside going forward.
 Overall, the bullish view remains intact. An eventual break above 18,050 can take the Nifty Smallcap 250 index up to 19,000 initially in the medium term.
 From a long-term perspective, the Nifty Smallcap 250 index has the potential to target 23,000 and 24,500 on the upside.
 As mentioned last week, the index will come under pressure only if breaks below 17,000. In that case, 16,000 or even 15,000 can be seen on the downside. However, that will not negate our long-term bullish outlook. It will only delay the expected rally to 23,000-24,500.
 Key supports 
 Nifty 50: 24,950-24,900
 Sensex: 81,000, 80,500
 Nifty Bank: 59,850
